name: EUCHRE
description: Euchre is the classic American partnership trick-taking game, played with a 24-32 card deck. Its hallmark feature is the 'Bower' system: the Jack of the called trump suit (Right Bower) and the Jack of the same-colored suit (Left Bower) are the two highest trump cards. Teams of two bid for the right to name trump and must win 3 of 5 tricks; failure results in being 'Euchred' and the opponent scoring 2 points. First team to 10 points wins.

content.text: Euchre is the classic American partnership trick-taking game, played with a 24-32 card deck. Its hallmark feature is the 'Bower' system: the Jack of the called trump suit (Right Bower) and the Jack of the same-colored suit (Left Bower) are the two highest trump cards. Teams of two bid for the right to name trump and must win 3 of 5 tricks; failure results in being 'Euchred' and the opponent scoring 2 points. First team to 10 points wins.

Euchre developed in the early 19th century American Midwest. It is believed to derive from 'Jucker' or 'Juckerspiel,' a card game played by German immigrants in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and Indiana. It was the dominant American card game before Poker took over in the late 19th century.
24 cards: 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each of 4 suits (Euchre deck). Some use 28 (add 7s and 8s) or 32 cards.
24-card Euchre deck. Score markers or score paper.

items.text: Canadian Euchre: Uses 52-card deck. Played in Ontario and Maritime Canada.
Buck Euchre: 4-6 player individual variant with no fixed partnerships.
